annotations.title: Add or correct a unit of measure, or set the currency

description: Teach this document a unit it does not know — `slice`, `IU`, a tablespoon that is 20 ml in this kitchen. A unit is what a declared column says its figures are in and what a claim's `in` converts into, so a conversion the document cannot make is a conversion this fixes. **The engine converts inside a dimension and never across one**: grams to kilograms is arithmetic, millilitres to grams needs a density, and a density is a column of the format rather than a unit. A symbol the document already has is corrected — its factor and its note, never what it measures. `currency` sets the document’s currency — what a new amount on a screen starts in; a row still names its own. `week_starts_on` is what `this week` counts from (Monday). `formats` lists them. Returns the diff and writes nothing until `commit: true`.

commit.description: Write it. Omit or false for the dry run.

currency.description: The document’s currency, a three-letter code: `ILS`.

path.description: Absolute path to a .emd file on this machine.

units.description: One object per unit. Up to 64 in a call; none for a setting alone.

dimension.description: What it measures. Needed for a unit this document has not got, and refused for one it has.

note.description: What it is, or which convention it follows. A tablespoon is 15 ml here and 20 ml in Australia, and this is what tells the next reader which.

per_base.description: How many of that dimension's base unit one of these is — g, ml, mm, s, kJ, each. A kilogram is 1000. Above zero.

symbol.description: As it is written on a column and after an `in` — `slice`, `µg`, `tbsp`. Letters and digits, no spaces, no arithmetic. Case matters: mg is not Mg.

name: record_units
title: Add or correct a unit of measure, or set the currency
